RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Reference number: POC-E2AA78E9EC-43782
Member: Harper Delgado (Member ID: W267205200)
Requested service: Knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery, CPT 29881
Date of denial notice: 2026-08-09
Appeal deadline: 2027-02-05 (within 180 days of the notice, per the terms stated in the denial letter)

To the Appeals & Grievances Department:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 29881 (knee arthroscopy with meniscectomy) for my knee condition, under the surgical care of Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery. The stated reason for denial was that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." I am submitting this appeal, along with the complete clinical documentation described below, to address that stated gap and to request that Harvard Pilgrim reverse the denial.

I understand that prior authorization review for knee surgeries is delegated by Harvard Pilgrim to its vendor, Evolent (formerly National Imaging Associates), and that the clinical criteria applied to this request are contained in Evolent's clinical guideline for knee arthroscopy. I have not been given the specific page or section of the guideline that was found lacking, and I have not personally been able to confirm the complete, exact wording of the guideline edition Harvard Pilgrim applied to my case on the date of this determination. I am not quoting or asserting that specific edition's language beyond what is set out below, which is text I was able to obtain from Evolent's own published materials on knee arthroscopy. I respectfully ask that Harvard Pilgrim identify, in its response to this appeal, the exact guideline title, number, and effective date it applied, and the specific documentation element(s) it considered missing, so that I may respond to any remaining gap.

The following clinical documentation, from the prior authorization packet, addresses the general categories of information that Evolent's own published materials on knee arthroscopy identify as necessary for review. Evolent's "Knee Arthroscopy Clinical Tip Sheet" states that "[o]ffice notes for arthroscopic knee surgery requests should document: Symptom onset, duration, and severity; Loss of function and/or limitations; Type and duration of non-operative management modalities (where applicable)." My record contains each of these elements:

1. Symptom onset, duration, and severity: 18 months of progressive knee pain, unrelieved by rest, with locking and giving way.

2. Loss of function and limitations: I am unable to squat or kneel and am limited to level walking. On examination, I have positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.

3. Non-operative treatment type and duration:
 - Supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, 14 weeks (2026-03-26 to 2026-07-02), 20 visits completed, documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
 - NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief.
 - Corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-13, giving only 2 weeks of partial relief.

This treatment history exceeds the non-operative treatment duration described in Evolent's tip sheet, which states that "[m]ost meniscal tears WILL require documentation of non-operative treatment as follows: Failure of at least 6 weeks of non-operative treatment, including at least two of the following: Rest or activity modifications/limitations; Ice/heat; Protected weight bearing; Pharmacologic treatment: oral/topical NSAIDS, acetaminophen, analgesics, tramadol; Brace/orthosis; Physical therapy modalities; Supervised home exercise; Weight optimization; Corticosteroid injection." My record documents at least four of these modalities (protected activity, NSAIDs, physical therapy, and corticosteroid injection) over 14 weeks and 4 months respectively — well beyond the minimum duration referenced.

In addition, my presentation independently qualifies under the exception to the non-operative treatment requirement described in the same Evolent materials: "History of acute injury/onset of symptoms with a locked knee and/or mechanical symptoms of locking; Physical examination demonstrates ANY positive meniscal findings on examination or demonstrates evidence of a locked knee (loss of terminal extension); MRI demonstrates a bucket-handle tear of the meniscus." My MRI of 2026-07-14 documents a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking, and my examination and reported symptoms (locking, giving way, inability to squat or kneel) directly correspond to this description.

Regarding radiographic workup, the same Evolent materials state that "[f]or meniscus surgery requests, if there is evidence of associated arthritis by history, physical examination or MRI, weight-bearing X-rays are required to further establish the degree of articular cartilage loss," but that "[u]nless the patient has a locked knee with a displaced bucket-handle tear, weight-bearing X-rays must show no more than mild arthritis for approval of meniscus procedures." My case involves a locked knee with a displaced bucket-handle tear, which places it within this stated exception. In any event, my MRI documents preserved articular cartilage and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1 findings, consistent with only mild degenerative change.

Finally, my record shows no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and non-smoker status, and my corticosteroid injection (2026-05-13) was administered well outside any pre-surgical injection window that may be specified in the applicable guideline.

For these reasons, I believe the complete clinical record — including the physical therapy discharge note, medication and injection history, the MRI report of 2026-07-14, and Dr. Reyes's examination findings — resolves the documentation gap cited in the denial and supports medical necessity for CPT 29881. I have asked Dr. Reyes's office to submit or resubmit these underlying records directly to Harvard Pilgrim/Evolent in support of this appeal; copies are also enclosed with this letter.

I request that Harvard Pilgrim:
1. Reverse the denial and authorize CPT 29881; or
2. If the denial is upheld, provide the specific guideline title, number, effective date, and section relied upon, and identify precisely what documentation remains missing, so that I may supply it or pursue further appeal, including external review through the Maine Bureau of Insurance if necessary.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and provide your decision within the timeframe required under Maine law and Harvard Pilgrim's appeal procedures.

Enclosures:

- Medication and injection records (NSAID trial; corticosteroid injection 2026-05-13)
